newsitem.title: JAPAN: AT&T plans low-cost international service in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: AT&T plans low-cost international service in Tokyo.

text.p: AT&T Communications Services Japan said on Wednesday it planned to launch a new low-cost international long-distance phone service in Tokyo to send voice data and faxes using its Worldwide Intelligent Network.
The company, a unit of AT&T Corp of the United States, did not say when the new service would start.
The service would initially only be offered to business customers but would be available to individual consumers in the near future, it said.
The rate for a three-minute call to Canada or the United States will be 240 yen for three minutes, which it said compared with 450 yen that was now being paid by Japanese customers.
Calls to Australia, Hong Kong and Taiwan would cost 420 yen for three minutes, which it said would be 210 to 300 yen less than the standard rate now available.
